newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- MARCH 26.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--The National Bank of Greece is planning a two-stage rescheduling of debts, sources report. National Bank Governor Theodoros Karatzas has reportedly already decided on tactics to be adopted, adjusted for the amount of the debt.

--There will be no additional taxation to boost tax revenues, according to National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou, but tax collection measures will be intensified. Problems in meeting budget targets will be dealt with by cutbacks in state spending rather than more taxes.

--The Capital Market Commission is consulting legal advisers on violations and irregularities noted in audits of listed members by three international houses recently, to give a legal basis to fines imposed.

--The balance of current accounts last year failed to live up to expectations, not only due to the hard drachma policy but to the "inappropriate" mix of economic policies followed by the government. Only infrastructural measures can boost the economy's competitiveness, according to the Bank of Greece.

--The Bank of Central Greece should be the first state-run bank to be sold by the summer, according to reports. The invitation for bids is expected to be published by the weekend with first offers in by the end of April.
--The Capital Market Commission is expected - probably on Wednesday - to announce fines on a series of listed members implicated in the Delta financial scandal to hit the Athens bourse last year.

--The finance ministry on Monday ruled out any further extension to the deadline for submission of tax declarations. Tax offices are expected to remain open in the afternoon of the last three days before the deadline of Friday March 28.
--The revised plan for the sale of state-run Cretabank is taking on its final form with the joint ministerial decision on the retendering of the bank expected to be published this week or early next.
--Experts say the state has no business holding reserves of up to one trillion drachmas. The amount in one fiscal year should not exceed 300 billion.

--The prime minister is reported to be preparing a reshuffle of his cabinet after the late April Easter break following recommendations from Environment, Town Planning and Public Works Minister Costas Laliotis. The prime minister is concerned by a shortfall in budget targets of 80 billion drachmas in the first two months with latest figures on the balance of payments worrying.
--Experts see foreign investors leading a new assault on the stock exchange next month, given the state of the economy. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4 (c) Reuters Limited 1997
